spec.description: Subscribe to trade events for one or more currency pairs. A push may batch multiple trades, which does not imply they resulted from a single taker order.

symbol.description: Currency pairs to subscribe to, e.g. `["BTC/USD", "MATIC/GBP"]`.

snapshot.description: Request a snapshot of the most recent 50 trades after subscribing.

channel.description: The channel this push belongs to.

type.description: Whether this push is the initial snapshot or an incremental update.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair, e.g. `"BTC/USD"`.

side.description: The side of the taker order.

ord_type.description: The order type of the taker order.

trade_id.description: Trade identifier -- a sequence number, unique per book.

notes: `data[].side` is left as a bare string per rule 2: unlike `ord_type` (which has an explicit 'One of: limit, market' tag on this page), trade.md documents no closed set for `side` -- no 'One of:' tag, just 'The side of the taker order.' Both worked examples show `buy`/`sell`, and the WS trading core (`trading_ws`) already types the *request*-side `side` as `Literal['buy', 'sell']` for `add_order`, but that is a different (request) field on a different endpoint; this page never closes the set for the *response* field, so it is not invented here.
